Perfume rating 4.16 out of 5 with 6,325 votes

Ari by Ariana Grande is a Floral Fruity Gourmand fragrance for women. Ari was launched in 2015. Top notes are Raspberry, Pear and Grapefruit; middle notes are Vanilla Orchid, Rose and Lily-of-the-Valley; base notes are Marshmallow, Musk and Woody Notes.

Pop singer Ariana Grande launches her first fragrance in September 2015 called Ari by Ariana Grande.

The fragrance is announced as luscious and sexy, opening with sparkling fruity notes connected to its ultra-feminine floral heart and the base of musk, woods and marshmallow accord.

It is available in a cute pink bottle with white pom-pom as 50 ml Eau de Parfum.

Saaara 09/18/25 22:51

I can't emphasize enough how much of a safe buy this one is.
This is the kind of feminine smell that all girls want to have at some stage.
Younger girls and teens can definitely wear this more easily but it's still not too juvenile to be a no-go for all adults.

Unfortunately, this took way too long for it to be detectable to me - when I first got it I couldn't smell a thing no matter how much I sprayed, where I sprayed and even smelling the bottle itself. Now, she's come out of her shell. It has some sort of nostalgic outdated smell to it that I can't explain yet continues to be such a safe reach and is a smell that makes others remember you. It's nice and sweet and very fruity. The marshmallow really isn't strong in this at all, in fact it's so light that I can hardly smell it over the juicy, almost sparkling fruitiness of it.

It's Moonlight's younger sister, but without Moonlight being much older. Only difference is Ari is way more lighter and softer and Moonlight uses a more bold fruit. Overall not my personal favourite AG perfume but certainly the first one I'd recommend anyone try especially because it will definitely easily capture attention of those constantly around you.

Do have to say, the projection is noticeably not the best and this scent gets quiet real fast, hard to detect on myself shortly after applying.

Ughh wearing this makes me feel younger without coming across as immature.

Honest review: Ari by Ariana Grande.

Initial Impression:
OUCH, my nose. Quickly runs away (A bit headache inducing). Wow, this smells like… everything LOL. Super powerhouse at first spritz, fistful of pear, marshmallows, vanilla, raspberry, some spice with a fistful of musk on roids. Non gourmand.

Dry Down:
The dry down consists of all notes all at once with the vanilla & marshmallows becoming the dominant notes as every hour goes by but this is a very ‘everything’ type of perfume. There is a lot going on, the best way I can compare this smell is if you walk into a perfume shop, that’s what Ari smells like. Non gourmand.

Application:
A few spritzes last throughout the day and towards shower time at night. If I spray my jacket with Ari by Ariana Grande, I’d smell it for a few days.

This is a girly perfume but I’d envision all ages to be using this, this is a very playful scent so if you’re looking for something more mature, you could layer over another perfume more vanilla dominant. I adore this perfume, great for when I’m feeling extroverted because the sillage on this is astronomical lol.

Hope this helps! ❤️

lxsia 03/30/25 12:33

Ari by Ariana Grande: Sweet, Playful Perfection (Especially for the Younger Crowd!)

Okay, let's talk about Ari by Ariana Grande. This perfume holds a special place in my heart because it was gifted to me during my high school days, and it instantly became my signature scent. And honestly? It still makes me smile!

Ari is the epitome of sweet, feminine, and playful. It's like a burst of sugary goodness in a bottle. Think fluffy marshmallows, juicy raspberries, and a touch of creamy vanilla. It's the kind of scent that instantly lifts your mood and makes you feel effortlessly girly.

This is the perfect everyday fragrance. It's light enough to wear to class, but still has enough personality to make you feel confident and put-together. It's not a mature scent by any means, so if you're looking for something sophisticated and complex, this might not be your jam. But if you want a fun, flirty, and undeniably sweet fragrance, Ari is a winner.

The price point is also fantastic. It's incredibly affordable, especially for a celebrity fragrance. And the longevity? Surprisingly good! It lasts a decent amount of time, especially on clothes. I've gotten compliments on it throughout the day, which is always a plus.

It's important to note that this is definitely a youthful scent. It's perfect for high school and college students, or anyone who loves a sweet, playful fragrance. It's like a carefree, sugary hug in a bottle.

If you're a younger person looking for a sweet, feminine, and affordable everyday scent, I highly recommend Ari. It's a classic for a reason, and it's sure to become a staple in your collection. Just be prepared to smell absolutely delicious!

CandiedPlumeria 01/16/25 15:37

ariana grande's debut fragrance, ari, reminds me of a particular sort of femininity, one which may seem slightly outdated, yet is simultaneously effortless, inspirational, and perhaps somewhat attainable... soft, brunette hair, cozy, neutral-toned sweaters, skinny jeans, high-heeled boots, simple, silver jewelry, matte lipstick, winged eyeliner, and perfectly-shaped eyebrows. if ari was a song, it would be roses by the chainsmokers.

ari opens up with a fresh, sweet, almost tart burst of fruits, mostly raspberry and grapefruit, and quickly makes way for what i would consider to be the star of the show... marshmallow, warm, sweet, and cozy marshmallow. after it dries down, bright, fresh fruits, slight, subtle florals, and musk are present, and detectable, but what i mostly get is warm, sweet, fruity marshmallow. everything in ari is well-balanced to create a generally sweet, warm, enjoyable scent. after a couple of hours, it grows more slight, and more powdery.

ariana grande's sweet like candy is a powdery, sugar-y, marshmallow overload, a perfume which seems to could only have been concocted in candyfornia, but ari isn't excessively sweet, it feels slightly more mature, and feels more feminine as opposed to girly. i find it to be quite versatile, it could work for a younger girl, but it certainly wouldn't feel out-of-place on a young adult, or someone older. it feels most appropriate for colder weather, but i feel like it could also work in warmer weather, also. it isn't challenging, so you could easily wear ari on a day-to-day basis, for many different occasions, it could even work as a signature scent.

ari's longevity isn't fantastic, but not to the point where it takes away from my enjoyment of the fragrance. it's very easy for me to wear, as it's just a very pleasant, sweet scent, that feels feminine, pretty, and makes me feel like the kind of woman i want to be, which i love.

kittenpawz 04/17/24 10:32

One of the perfumes in the "reminds me of" section is Gucci Flora Gorgeous Gardenia which I couldn't wear because of the soil-like smell of patchouli in it. Ari is unbelievably similar to Gorgeous Gardenia without the patchouli. It was a blind buy and these two being listed as similar perfumes was one of the reasons for me to get it because I was looking for a fix-it perfume, having been partially fascinated by Gorgeous Gardenia nonetheless. It is undeniably more synthetic-smelling but not enough to put you off if you typically go for stuff like Pink Sugar or Britney Spears perfumes. Ari is everything Gorgeous Gardenia could have been: sweet, nymphet-like, soft, clean and dreamy. The drydown reminds me a lot of Miss Dior EDP 2021 with how musky-vanilla it is. I would also draw some parallels between Ari and the smell of makeup for teenagers from 2000s which is what the synthetic note in this perfume is reminiscent of. Overall I like it.

As I sprayed it, my mom reprimanded me for my perfume being to sweet. To each their own because I don't think it's too much - I expected sweeter. This is hardly unbearably sweet, a happy medium if you compare it to the likes of Pink Sugar or LDBS. So if you're in the mood for something super saccharine, this isn't exactly that. It's also inoffensive and watery like an EDT and lacks intensity for my personal taste, but it's definitely a cut above most celeb frags. It doesn't smell refined, sure, but nor is it annoyingly cheap. And for what it's worth, it's easier to find AG perfumes on sale as opposed to perfumes of house Dior or Gucci. If you can get a good deal, why the heck not?

So yeah. Putting the chronological order of these perfumes' release aside: two duds Miss Dior EDP 2021 and Gucci Flora Gorgeous Gardenia had a baby that is Ari, and the baby, not without flaws of her own of course, managed to get only the good traits from them. Then she got under cool aunty Pink Sugar's influence and the rest is history.

It's hard for me to pick out the specific fruity/floral notes in this but I can for sure smell the marshmallow and woods & subtle musk of the drydown. It all blends so smoothly and smells classy yet flirty and very feminine. I think this smells more similar to moonlight than sweet like candy....SLC is my absolute favorite btw. Bad taste in a bottle. I saw this one on a shelf and wanted to try it.

Never, ever again without a strip of paper first!

It smells so acrid and harsh, very loud in the opening with a head-hammering "fruit" edge. No, this is not fruit at all! Please, go to a market, smell every fruit and register in your brain what fruits they are.
Raspberry? No way. Raspberry is a lovely fruit with a typical acidity that you may like or not, but it's real! Chemical grapefruit smells like armpit.
I think I left some of my carefully kept neurons on this "scent", burned down through my nose.
Vanilla orchid? If Cartier So Pretty were still alive, you would know what a vanilla orchid smells like, even when fake.
And marshmallow... plus generic maybe Woods... oh, yes, and "musk".
A cheap mess probably assembled by a machine.
I had to keep it on my wrist and sleeve and I could see its "evolution"
A head banging that is short-lived, but never enough.
